rationale: S5 (#419): a template-LOCAL binding whose name collides with a SAME-NAMED MEMBER must shadow it. Here `{#each rows as row}` binds `row`, `{#each nested as group} {#each group.children as item}` binds inner `item`, and `{@const total = r.id}` binds `total` — all three names are ALSO member functions. The template body reads the LOCAL binding, so NO `uses` edge to the member `row`/`item`/`total` may be emitted. Only the collection expressions (`rows`, `nested`) are member uses. (The wave's template-member-uses fixture never exercised a real collision, so this shadow rule shipped unproven at the actual bug class — the vue V4 lesson.)
